# audit

**Time Modulators · Consolidated family**

## Intuition

Keep the latest value while waiting for a duration signal.

## Specification

The first value starts waiting. Later values replace the stored value without restarting the duration. A duration next emits the stored value; silent duration completion does not.

### Lifetime and policy details

A source completion can wait for an active duration. A duration error fails the output. Downstream cancellation closes both subscriptions. See the [audit scenarios](/guide/audit-scenarios).

### Names represented

`audit`, `auditTime`.

### Configuration vocabulary

- `withTime(milliseconds, scheduler?)`
- `withSignal(durationSelector)`

These are available forms and modifiers, not a list to combine indiscriminately. See the [migration guide](/MIGRATION) for supported combinations and signatures.

## Example

This is a wiring sketch: streams and application functions such as `source$`, `isValid`, or `load` are supplied by your application. Import operators from `rxjs-80`, controls from `rxjs-80/controls`, and supporting types, Subjects, and schedulers from `rxjs`.

```typescript
source$.pipe(audit(withTime(250)))
```

Building this expression does not subscribe. Connect a consumer to start the Observable execution; a live producer may already exist independently. [Run a complete example](/guide/getting-started#first-pipeline).
